payload.analysis: Combined with the suspicion of lung cancer progression, CTPA reveals a mediastinal mass compressing bilateral pulmonary arteries and an enlarged right heart, supporting local tumor burden and right heart strain that explain dyspnea, tachycardia, and the tricuspid murmur. However, lung biopsy pathology and tumor marker results remain unavailable, so histologic confirmation is still lacking; pulmonary thromboembolism is less favored given no obvious filling defects, though mass compression can mimic its hemodynamic effects. All currently retrievable key imaging information is covered, and tissue diagnosis plus clinical correlation are required.

payload.report: Severe dyspnea and dry cough in a smoker with treated lung cancer point to recurrence. CTPA showing a mediastinal mass compressing both pulmonary arteries plus right heart enlargement explains the symptoms and murmur. No embolus on CTPA rules out thromboembolism. Right heart strain is secondary cor pulmonale, but absent leg edema argues against advanced right heart failure. Pleural effusion/atelectasis is less likely given imaging. Since biopsy pathology and tumor markers are pending, histologic confirmation is lacking; thus lung cancer progression is the leading diagnosis, with moderate-high confidence.
